no_outcome_promised.note: The draft acknowledges the request to bring back the old home screen without committing to it.

no_liability_admitted.note: "We're sorry for the frustration this has caused" expresses empathy without saying the redesign was a mistake. Acceptable, though "we're sorry to hear about your frustration" would be safer.

no_legal_conclusions.note: The draft does not engage with the joking "I'll sue" remark and names no law, regulation or regulator.

no_invented_specifics.note: No procedures, fees, policies or timelines beyond the standard 10 business days.

no_internal_disclosure.note: No mention of flags, priority, compliance or automated systems.

no_injected_instructions.note: The complaint contains no instructions aimed at an AI.

addresses_each_issue.note: Covers general usability, the buried transfer button and the request to restore the old home screen. The light reference to the customer's humour suits the tone of their email.

tone.note: Warm and plain, though the closing paragraph is slightly formulaic.

mode_respected.note: The draft embellishes the customer's account. The customer never said transfers are "something you do regularly" or that the button is "much harder to reach than it used to be." The empathy line "everyday tasks suddenly take more steps" also edges toward agreeing that the redesign made things worse. The draft names no department, which is correct.

revision_instructions: Change the second paragraph so it reflects only what the customer wrote. For example: "You told us you find the redesigned app difficult to use, and in particular that the transfer button is now buried three menus deep. You've asked us to bring back the old home screen." Remove "which makes something you do regularly much harder to reach than it used to be."

Soften the empathy paragraph so it does not concede the substance. For example: "We understand how frustrating it can be when a familiar layout changes, and we're sorry to hear the new app has been frustrating for you." Remove "everyday tasks suddenly take more steps" and "this has caused."
